# Was the FBI's NCIC crime database hacked?

**Not established.** CNN, NBC News, AP and ABC News, each citing their own unnamed sources, report the FBI is investigating an apparent hack. the President called it 'not good' without details. The FBI has not commented.

Incident: FBI crime database (NCIC) intrusion, reported Nov 20, 2026. Also reported as the NCIC breach and the FBI crime database hack. First published Nov 20, 2026; last updated Nov 21, 2026, 8:19 PM ET.

> **Not verified: initial investigation only.** Nothing on this page is absolutely confirmed. It is an early look based only on publicly available sources, and it should not be treated as verified fact. Even items labeled "Confirmed" only mean a public source reports them. ## At a glance

- Status: monitoring
- Size: Nation-level potential. NCIC is used by more than 100,000 criminal justice partners nationwide. No source says what was reached, so this is the worst case, not a known impact.
- Who is affected: Potentially police and courts that rely on NCIC, and people with records in it. No source says whose records, if any, were reached, and there is no notice for the public to act on.

### Known so far

- CNN, NBC News, AP and ABC News, each citing their own unnamed sources, report the FBI is investigating an apparent breach of NCIC.
- NCIC is the FBI-run database police nationwide use for warrants, stolen property and other records.
- The FBI has not commented on the reports.
- the President called the reported hack 'not good' on Nov 21 but gave no details.
- A separate breach hit the FBI jobs site in September; the FBI blamed a contractor's missed patch.

### Not known yet

- Whether the FBI confirms the breach. The reports rest on unnamed sources, and the President's remarks gave no details.
- What part of NCIC was reached, how the intruders got in, and who they are.
- Whether any records were copied or changed.
- Whether it is linked to this week's outages or the September jobs-site breach. No source says so.
- Whether NCIC service for police was interrupted.

## What we checked and did not find

We looked for these and did not find them as of about 8:20 PM ET on Nov 21, 2026.

- An FBI or Justice Department statement about NCIC (the FBI press releases page has none).
- A White House or congressional statement about the reported intrusion. the President commented in an interview but gave no details.
- An on-record official confirming the intrusion. NBC News, AP and ABC News have their own unnamed sources; Reuters, WUSA9, BleepingComputer and others repeat CNN.
- Any detail on what was accessed, how, by whom, or whether records were changed.
- A claim of responsibility.
- Any official link between NCIC and this week's outages, or the September jobs-site breach.
- Any report that NCIC service for police was interrupted.
